3	This client carries workarounds for bugs/gaps in the control-plane
4	OpenAPI document and its surface. Each item below should be fixed at the

12	## 1. Operations enumerate every error status with no shared `default`
13	
14	**Symptom:** each operation declares its real success code (good — 201
15	for creates, 200 for reads, 204 for deletes) but then lists every error
16	status separately (`400`, `401`, `403`, `422`, `500`, …) with no
17	`default` response. ogen turns that into a per-operation sum-type result,
18	forcing a type switch at every call site instead of the ergonomic
19	`(*T, error)`.
20	
21	**Fix upstream:** emit a single `default` error response (every error
22	already references the same `ErrorModel`, so a `default` is lossless).
23	ogen then generates "convenient errors" — `(*T, error)` with non-2xx as a
24	typed `*ErrorModelStatusCode` — straight from the spec.
25	
26	**Workaround:** `spec/normalize.go` (`foldErrorResponses`) folds each
27	operation's explicit 4xx/5xx into one `default`, keeping the real success
28	code untouched. This is the one transform that is a deliberate
29	ergonomics choice rather than a pure bug workaround; a shared `default`
30	upstream retires it.
31

The fresh pull regresses the build. The committed `origin/main` spec contains `GrantMirrorCollaborator` (and the CLI depends on it + `RevokeMirrorCollaborator`), but the live upstream at `us.console.entire.io` no longer emits those operations — so regenerating drops them and `cmd/entire/cli` no longer compiles. content.text:
Confirmed the mechanism: `origin/main`'s committed spec has `post`+`delete` on `/mirrors/collaborators` (the grant/revoke ops the CLI calls), but live upstream only serves `get`. Those two ops were hand-authored into the vendored spec **ahead of upstream deployment** — pulling fresh drops them and breaks `cmd/entire/cli`.

So a clean "pull fresh" can't be committed as-is. Your real ask (nicely-formatted vendored spec) doesn't actually require a fresh pull — I can reformat the *existing* committed spec through `jq .` with zero content change. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Pull fresh as-is
options.description: Commit the live spec unchanged, accepting a broken cmd/entire/cli build until upstream deploys the endpoints. Not advised.

content.text:
Done. Committed on fresh branch `vendor/openapi-jq-format` (off `origin/main`), not pushed.

**Bottom line:** Refresh docs now pipe through `jq .`; vendored spec reformatted to 8456 lines. A true "pull fresh" was **not safe** — I reformatted the existing spec instead.

- **Why not a live pull:** live upstream (`us.console.entire.io`) no longer serves the `post`/`delete` on `/mirrors/collaborators` (`grantMirrorCollaborator`/`revokeMirrorCollaborator`). Those were hand-authored into the committed spec ahead of deployment; a fresh pull drops them and breaks `cmd/entire/cli`. (I asked how to proceed; you were away, so I took the safe path.)
- **What I committed:** `jq .` in the refresh docs (`gen.go`, `normalize.go`) + the existing `core.openapi.json` pretty-printed in place. Content is byte-identical modulo whitespace — verified via `jq -S` diff; regeneration produced zero changes to `core.gen.json` or the generated Go.
- **Verified:** `go build ./...` OK, `mise run fmt` clean, `mise run lint` 0 issues.

If you want the actual upstream refresh, we need to either re-graft the grant/revoke ops each time or wait for upstream to ship them — say the word and I'll do the re-graft variant.
what we can do is create a PR with base https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1602, that will mean no ogen changes, just the jq formatting machinery.
